findings:
CONTEXT: There are two separate lines of theory work. They use the same words but they are different engines.
(1) A runtime bend-state model for CAD-matched bends, from March 2026: the factor model / count posterior.
(2) The later "F1" bend-LINE detection research (zero-shot PLY first, then CAD-guided), scored against Gold line references.
Most of the theory docs describe (1). Most of the recent effort and every recent F1 number belong to (2).

1. INTENDED MODEL FOR COMPLETE vs INCOMPLETE SCANS (docs/BEND_STATE_FACTOR_MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md)
- The core idea is to stop using one flat 4-way label (FORMED/NOT_FORMED/PARTIALLY_OBSERVED/UNOBSERVED). Instead each CAD bend i gets three separate things (lines 8-12, 35-53):
  - C_i: whether the bend is physically completed (binary in v1; a continuous hinge/angle is a later extension).
  - rho_i: a continuous visibility score built from CAD ray-casting, local support, density and alignment stability.
  - A_i: which local evidence candidate the bend is assigned to, with an explicit null option.
- The four user-facing labels are derived from these, not modelled directly (lines 60-69).
- Factorization (line 108): p(C,A|x) ∝ ∏ψ_i(C_i,A_i;rho_i,g_i) ∏ψ_excl(A) ∏ψ_adj(C_i,C_j). It is CRF-style because the geometric features overlap and are not independent (lines 125-132).
- Learned parts: two calibrated gradient-boosted-tree heads, one for visibility and one for formed/not-formed. Logistic regression is kept as an ablation (lines 143-153).
- Coupling: hard exclusivity between confusable bends first; weak adjacency only later (lines 155-168).
- Count decoding: the completed count K is read from the posterior over K using its median, not from per-bend argmax or MAP (lines 196-210).
- Monotonicity across staged scans: count-only, through soft posterior regularization (lines 246-256).
- A process-stage variable S is optional and explicitly NOT a primary latent in v1 (lines 57-58, 167). The reason given is that stage metadata did not exist.
- Two principles that held up in testing (docs/MATH_PRECISION_RND_PLAN.md:125-148; docs/ONE_PAGER_PARTIAL_BEND_STATE_INFERENCE.md:34-36):
  - UNOBSERVED is missing evidence, not evidence of absence.
  - Global alignment quality does not prove that a given bend's neighbourhood was actually observed.
- Rejected after testing (MATH_PRECISION_RND_PLAN.md:150-157): stricter one-sided thresholds, geometry-weighted assignment, and global optimal assignment. The last one regressed 49024000_A.
- In this framework a complete scan is simply the case where every rho_i is high and every C_i is FORMED. No separate engine was designed for complete scans.

2. WHAT THE "PROFESSOR" ADVISED
- Provenance: the later packets are prompts that open "You are the professor responsible for selecting exactly one bounded next action…" (docs/research/2026-08-16_professor_post_v70_sparse_field_architecture_packet.md:3). Some files are named *_GPT56_PRO_PROMPT. So much of the "professor" is a prompted AI role. The March 2026 response's provenance is not stated in the docs.
- March 15 response (docs/PROFESSOR_RESPONSE_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE_20260315.md:8-50):
  - Use a CRF-style model with C_i/rho_i/A_i; no flat multiclass model and no stage latent in v1.
  - Two calibrated GBDT heads; GBDT before neural models.
  - Hard exclusivity over confusable evidence atoms.
  - Count from the median of the posterior over K; no separate count head.
  - Count-only soft monotonicity.
  - Diagnosis (lines 72-80): the main error is wrong assignment structure when visibility is partial.
- March 29 response, the system doctrine (docs/research/PROFESSOR_RESPONSE_SYNTHESIS_20260329.md):
  - Split three kinds of truth: which bends exist, what nominal geometry to compare against, and what this scan can actually observe (lines 11-18).

  - Truth basis: the manufacturing operation decides target inventory and progress counting; the released nominal decides acceptance (lines 41-46).
  - Datum-island alignment (lines 48-66). For partial parts: the largest invariant flat plus holes/slots on it, then stable edges, then already-completed panels tied back to that flat. Remove unconstrained global ICP from the metrology path first.
  - A ternary state FORMED/UNFORMED/UNKNOWN, with UNKNOWN the default on partial scans (lines 78-86).

IMPLEMENTED (runtime path):

NOT IMPLEMENTED:
- Count monotonicity / staged prior (Backlog Phase 4).
- Any bend-order or sequence prior. rg finds no bend_order use in backend/domains except a disclaimer flag in backend/vendor_manufacturing_job.py:128.
- Datum-island registration as a formal objective.
- Formal section-based metrology.
- The per-bend ternary label corpus.
- The operator-save-rate metric.

CAD-guided F1 lane:
- Matched comparison on 11 cases: scan F1 .365 vs CAD fusion .458 (docs/research/2026-09-07_production_generalization_roadmap.md:223).
- Gold11 mesh-path physical runs emitted 0 lines (V2/V3).
  - Causes in V2: triangle numerical admission (9 cases), a 20M-membership cap (1 case), plane-proposal conditioning (1 case), and native ROI admission (2026-09-10_gold11_failure_factor_audit.md:45-56).
  - In V3, 18,541 proposed poses produced 0 refinement starts (lines 239-250).
- V11: control .4286 vs challenger .3818 (2026-09-16_gold11_v11_simple_family_failure_analysis.md:5-7). A 3-family subset reached F1 .818 at the 3 mm support gate and .917 at 5 mm (lines 68-74).
- 49001000 root cause: CAD STEP axes sit about 3–5 mm off the observed bend lines, and the 3 mm support gate rejects valid axes (lines 84-95).
- The roadmap (lines 9-26, 59-71) made CAD+scan offline the priority and deferred zero-shot. "Coupled uncertainty and per-characteristic partial output remain offline work" (line 71). The intended product contract has a stage-aware observed state (line 246).
- Unfolding exists only as a CAD-extraction byproduct: 6/20 selected-skin unfolds (docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md:199, 238-239). There is no flat-pattern INPUT.

WHY CAD SHOWED LITTLE GAIN (inference)
- CAD was used as a candidate-line prior to recover Gold bend LINES. It was never used as a stage-aware nominal for a known partial state, since the blind contract forces state=unknown.
- Native axes are systematically offset by about 3–5 mm, so CAD placement adds as many false positives as true positives.

4. MOST PROMISING UNEXECUTED IDEAS (ranked)
(a) Bend-order prefix hypothesis decoding for incomplete scans.
- With a tagged order of P מהלך phase groups, the admissible states shrink from 2^N per-bend combinations to P+1 prefixes.
- Replace the independent Poisson-binomial (bend_unary_model.py:683) with a likelihood per prefix hypothesis k (0..P). For each k, synthesize the intermediate nominal (flat pattern with the first k phases folded), align the scan to it with datum islands, and score the scan against each candidate. Pick by posterior, abstain if ambiguous, and allow a slack/out-of-order state.
- The architecture doc deferred a stage latent only because there was no metadata (lines 57, 167). Onboarding will now provide that metadata.
(b) Use the unfolded/flat file (or the CAD unfold) plus the bend order to generate the intermediate-stage CAD. This also gives each partial hypothesis its invariant datum region: the base panel plus already-formed panels.
(c) Professor section metrology: multi-slice sections orthogonal to the CAD bend line, frame anchored on the parent panel, median aggregation. The same sections directly yield flange length (bend line to flange edge) and bend position, both currently missing.
(d) A scan-derived centerline fit around each CAD axis (V11 analysis:97-103) to remove the 3–5 mm offset.
(e) The two-plane/finite-context pose proposals (failure audit:153-158) are designed but not built.
(f) Collect per-bend FORMED/UNFORMED/UNKNOWN labels and adopt operator review save rate as the metric. The tagged bend order plus the known stage per scan makes these labels cheap to derive.
(g) Count monotonicity applies only if the same part is scanned at several stages.

implications_for_production: Neither engine models the incomplete-scan case the user needs. The runtime count posterior assumes bends are independent (Poisson-binomial at backend/bend_unary_model.py:683), and the F1 CAD lane runs blind with state=unknown. The tagged bend order with מהלך phase groups is the missing piece: decoding over the P+1 phase-prefix hypotheses replaces the 2^N per-bend combinations, and is the single most promising change.

Adding the unfolded/flat-part upload to intake gives more than nicer display. Together with the bend order, it lets the engine build the intermediate-stage nominal geometry for each prefix hypothesis k. The scan can then be aligned and compared against what the part should look like after k phases, not against the finished CAD. This also gives each hypothesis its invariant datum region (base panel plus already-formed panels), which is the datum-island alignment the professor advised for partial parts.
Complete scans are just the case where the full-prefix hypothesis wins. They should share the same pipeline, with a high-coverage check and no separate engine.

Flange length, the operator's top need, is measured nowhere today. The professor's section-based metrology (multi-slice cross-sections orthogonal to the CAD bend line, frame anchored on the parent panel, median aggregation) would give flange length, angle and bend position from the same slices. It is designed but never built.

CAD-guidance showed no clear gain because CAD was used as a bend-line candidate prior scored against Gold lines, and native STEP axes sit about 3-5 mm off the observed lines (V11 analysis:84-95). Before relying on CAD axes for positions, fit a scan-derived centerline around each CAD axis.

The unary state head was trained on only 4 negatives, and partial-scan MAE stayed at 3.6 with or without the structured model. Collecting per-bend FORMED/UNFORMED/UNKNOWN labels, cheap once the bend order and stage are known, is the highest-value data step the professor named.

Measure success by operator review save rate at a fixed false-accept ceiling plus per-bend flange-length, angle and position error, not count MAE or line F1. Keep UNKNOWN as the default when a bend is not observable; never fill it from CAD.

Owner's own caveat: the existing unfolded parts were reverse-engineered from the folded CAD, so they cannot validate unfold-based stage synthesis yet. Real customer flat files (DXF/flat STEP) are needed for that.

implications_for_production: The only CAD-assisted lane with real benefit is the simple one: register the scan, project the CAD bend axes, then verify each against raw scan support. It gave scan+CAD F1 0.458 vs 0.365 scan-only on the same cases, and 0.82–0.92 F1 on simple families. Every heavy rebuild (V5 to V11) produced zero output. Production should build on the cheap projection-plus-verification path, not cad_guided v18.

The documented blocker in the CAD path is a systematic 3–5 mm offset between the CAD bend axis and the scan-observed bend line. The fix proposed on 16 Sep (fit a scan-derived centerline or contact line around each CAD axis) was never done. The same fix is also the basis for measuring flange length and position.
Development-fit scores (0.967 Shaked-12, 1.000 Gold-27) did not transfer: 2/9 and 3/4 on unseen parts, and F1 0.197 prospectively on 28 new scans. Any production claim needs a locked held-out cohort.

The owner's sense that CAD guidance gave 'no measurable gain' is partly a measurement artifact. The 27 Aug comparison of 0.518 vs 0.456 used different datasets. Matched, CAD fusion gained +0.093 F1, and exact count rose from 0/11 to 1/11 (EXP8 reached 4/11). Recall, not precision, is where CAD helps.

CAD-side bend extraction is now strong: 94.5% capture and 100% precision on 20 CADs, plus 12/12 on an unseen STEP. That makes CAD the right source for the expected bend list, angles and flange dimensions at onboarding. SLDPRT input is unsupported, so STEP is required.

Incomplete (mid-sequence) scans have never been evaluated. Codex flagged on 23 Sep that a finished CAD cannot be rigidly aligned to a partly bent part. Partial scans need per-flange or local registration driven by the tagged bend order and the k formed bends.

Unfold is preview-only (6/20 models). Since the owner's flat files are reverse-engineered from the folded CAD, an uploaded flat part should be treated as optional display and bend-ID aid, not as validated truth.

Process lesson: the owner repeatedly hit long audit or consultation cycles with no engine output, including multi-hour Gold11 runs that returned null. Production work needs fast single-scan end-to-end loops and visual checks before full-corpus runs. Note that a scan used to process in about 30 s; the V11 path took over 6 h for 11 scans.

(3) Stage truth for incomplete scans: the tagged bend order plus completed_bend_ids per scan, with a formed/unformed/unknown state. UNKNOWN counts as abstention, not as an error.

- state accuracy on partials;
- abstention/coverage;
- false-accept rate on defective (X) parts — the V/X pairs are useful here;
- worst-family results;
- latency.
Assignment goes by CAD ID after registration, so the 5°/4 mm line matcher becomes a secondary localization check.
(5) A prospective untouched cohort: at least 30 scans across at least 15 families, with complete and partial scans of the same parts, frozen before any tuning.
Current evaluators cover only (3)'s count proxy and line localization. The angle MAE exists only in the older regression pipeline. Flange length is unmeasured everywhere.

The truth on hand is mostly bend counts and manual 3D bend lines, much of it single-reviewer or assistant-made. Measured actual flange lengths and angles from a reference instrument do not exist, so production accuracy claims cannot currently be validated.

Partial-scan truth is weak. Most partial scans lack a confirmed completed count or completed_bend_ids, and the count-error mass is concentrated on partials. Incomplete-scan evaluation needs the tagged bend order plus a per-stage completed_bend_ids label (the incoming manifest template already has this field).

No real unfolded/flat files exist locally; flat views today are derived by unfolding the folded STEP (6/20 succeed). Adding a flat-file upload at onboarding is a new data source and gives a stable bend-ID anchor for both tagging and evaluation. Until real flat files arrive, any flat-file evaluation would be circular, because the flats were reverse-engineered from the folded CAD.

Every local physical scan (about 40 incoming plus about 30 in source-assets) is DEVELOPMENT_CONSUMED. A credible acceptance benchmark needs a prospectively sealed cohort: at least 30 scans across at least 15 families, opaque IDs, two independent annotators, and both complete and partial scans of the same parts. EHO4 and N001-N014 are the only reserved or opaque material.

The good/defective V/X pairs from the July-August Shaked deliveries are the only basis for measuring false acceptance, which an operator-facing pass/fail per bend needs. They should be annotated with per-bend measured values.

The status file kind is SHERMAN_QC_F1_PROGRAM_STATUS_V2, with objective "PRODUCTION_READY_ZERO_SHOT_SCAN_ONLY_AND_CAD_ASSISTED_BEND_INSPECTION" (docs/research/artifacts/f1_program_status_current.json). There is no single module called "the F1 engine". The engine is a chain of versioned stages (V16..V73), and every reported "F1" number is a line-detection score. None of them measures angle, length or flange accuracy.

implications_for_production: The production worker does not run the F1 research engine. It runs a separate CAD-driven RANSAC detector and greedy matcher (feature_detection/bend_detector.py). Integrating F1 means building a new adapter. It cannot be switched on with a flag.

F1 outputs only bend-line segments (start/end) and is scored only on line-localization F1. It produces no per-bend angle, radius or flange length. The operator's top need, flange length, must come from elsewhere. The closest existing code is the runtime BendMatch expected_/measured_edge_distance_mm (bend_detector.py:2340-2360).

Best physical evidence is weak: scan-only V51 reaches F1 0.593 on 12 consumed scans, and the Gold37 program-level result is 0.327. Selection/ownership, not candidate birth, is the bottleneck (pool ceiling recall 0.85).

The CAD-guided lane did help on matched cases (0.365 to 0.458 on Gold11). The owner's 'no gain' impression comes from comparing different corpora, which the Aug-27 audit rejects. CAD works as a constrained prior, not as an autonomous detector.

No code consumes bend order, מהלך groups, an unfolded/flat part, or an explicit partial state. scan_state is never passed by the worker, and partial-scan handling only tweaks fallback. Incomplete-scan support (first k of N bends) needs new state-conditioned matching: only bends 1..k of the CAD should be expected, and the later ones treated as legitimately unformed.

Given a known CAD, a known bend sequence and a scanner frame, the scan-only zero-shot detection problem F1 attacks is much harder than needed. A CAD-per-bend local measurement design (registered per-flange plane fits around each expected bend, gated by sequence step) fits the production target better than promoting V51.

F1 resource profile: P95 ~390 s and ~1.5 GB per scan (V52); the structured lane needs up to ~2.5 GB. The cad_guided v18 lane takes 10-20 min per scan. All of these are too slow and brittle for a per-part robotic-cell loop without redesign.

Governance: production_promotion_authorized=false, both lanes are RED, the 16 physical scans are still not downloaded, and 133 F1 backend modules plus 472 scripts are largely untracked. Freeze one candidate and retire the rest before any integration.

SCOPE: read-only source/docs survey of /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/FullProject. Nothing was executed and no raw CAD or scan bytes were opened.

1. WHAT EXISTS: THREE SEPARATE UNFOLD PATHS, ALL CAD-DERIVED. NONE INGESTS A USER FLAT FILE.
(a) Visual "selected-skin development", the one the UI uses. backend/vendor_unfold_preview.py:1-6 says it is "NOT a neutral-axis blank". It has no K-factor, no allowance and unverified units. It develops one skin (inner or outer surface) of the folded STEP as a tree of planes and cylinders. In _develop_faces (vendor_unfold_preview.py:1004-1110) the root is the largest planar face. For each bend, _child_transform (lines 921-941) builds a rigid hinge transform: rotation by -delta about the cylinder axis, plus translation R*delta along the tangent. Transforms compose parent-to-child down the tree. Each bend emits bend_lines {feature_id, line_start/end, bend_direction:"unknown", sweep_deg} (lines 1081-1083), and the flat flange overlays keep the same feature_id. Refusal gates: PARENT/CHILD_FLANGE_EXTENDS_INTO_DEVELOPED_BEND, seam closure, overlap, cyclic graph, sweep <=175 deg. Successors V4 to V6 exist: finite-width, coplanar stitch, native V6 (vendor_unfold_preview_v6.py, vendor_unfold_native_v6.py, vendor_cad_unfold_pipeline_v4.py). The API wires only workers v1 to v4, picked by env SHERMAN_VENDOR_UNFOLD_RUNTIME (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:211-218, 252-260). Unset means the legacy v1 worker. V5/V6 and the pipelines are research-only.
(b) Manufacturing draft, separate and offline. backend/vendor_manufacturing_job.py:1-6, 288-380 runs pinned FreeCAD 1.1.3 + SheetMetal 0.8.23 raw unfold, gated by a compensation profile with K-factor: BA = theta*(Ri + K*t). It emits analytic DXF (cut_dxf, bend_guide_dxf) and a bend_ledger with real up/down bend_direction, sweep, included angle and BA (vendor_manufacturing_freecad.py:523-546). Native markers are bound to vendor bend IDs by an exact-endpoint bijection with 1e-7 mm tolerance (vendor_manufacturing_bridge.py:41-75). It is not imported by the server. Evidence is synthetic only: V1b had 13 geometry oracles pass, V2 failed 56/57, and the V3 file workflow passed 4/4 synthetic (docs/operations/vendor-manufacturing-unfold-2026-09-29.md). manufacturing_ready and cut_release are hard false. No physical CAD has been run.
(c) Folded flange preview (expected flange length source). backend/vendor_flange_preview.py:334-386 measures nominal_flange_depth_mm, the "CAD_TANGENT_TO_OUTER_EDGE" distance (lines 188-288). It requires one straight outer rail parallel to the bend axis and equal depth on both skins; otherwise it returns null with UNAVAILABLE_AMBIGUOUS_BOUNDARY. This is the only CAD-side expected-flange-length producer in the setup path. It is disabled whenever a controlled unfold runtime is set (vendor_setup_service.py:237-240).

- Partial scans are handled by counting. bend_unary_model._count_posterior_summary (backend/bend_unary_model.py:683-741) takes a Poisson-binomial over independent per-bend formed-probabilities, which ignores the tagged order. Unobserved bends on partial scans get zero mass (lines 698-720).
- The draft has completed_steps (vendor_setup_service.py:73, validated at :201; UI stage stepper at VendorSetupPage.tsx:646). That is a planning field, not a per-scan input.

DESIGN PROPOSAL 1: INTAKE UI WITH FOLDED AND UNFOLDED VIEWS
(a) Add slot 4 next to CAD and Drawing: "Flat pattern (DXF / GEO / flat STEP)". Use a new route POST /api/parts/{id}/flat, modelled on upload_part_drawing. Store flat_file_path, flat_file_hash and flat_uploaded_at, and bind flat_file_hash into VendorSetupDraft beside drawing_file_hash.
(b) Parser: a bounded general DXF reader (ezdxf). Outer and inner loops come from LINE/ARC/LWPOLYLINE. Bend lines come from the TruTops layer convention plus any angle/direction TEXT/MTEXT (UP/DOWN) and radius. For flat STEP, take the single planar slab's face outline and the scribe/bend-line edges.
(c) Flat-to-folded bend binding. Cut the flat outline along the bend lines to get a panel graph, which must be a tree. Match it to the folded CAD flange/bend graph by node and edge count, bend-line length against the cylinder axial span, and adjacency. Then refine with a 2D rigid-plus-mirror ICP against the CAD skin development when one exists (6/20). Tolerances must allow the skin-versus-neutral gap of alpha*K*t per bend: about 0.94 mm at 90 deg, t=1.5, K=0.4.
(d) Unresolved matches (symmetric parts) go to operator confirmation: click a flat line, then the matching folded bend. A stored bijection replaces the vendorUnfoldDraft "all marks must be cad_candidate" rule. Precedence: uploaded flat first (it covers the 14/20 that refuse), CAD-developed flat second, folded only last.
(e) Bonus: a shop flat is a real blank, so the measured panel-to-bend-line distances back-solve the shop's effective BA/K per bend. That yields an independent expected flange length where vendor_flange_preview returns null.
(f) Caveat: the owner's current flats were reverse-engineered from the folded CAD, so they are circular and cannot validate any of this. Real shop DXFs are needed.

DESIGN PROPOSAL 2: EXPECTED GEOMETRY AFTER THE FIRST k BENDS
Admissible states are prefixes of the tagged sequence, cut only at מהלך group boundaries. That gives at most n+1 hypotheses instead of 2^n.
- Method A (recommended for coverage): hinge-rotate the folded CAD.
  1. Build the face tree from the folded STEP mesh: remove each bend cylinder's triangles via tessellation FACE_OCCURRENCE_RANGES (as vendor_flange_preview already does).
  2. Take axis and sweep from extract_step_bend_axes (94% bend capture).
  3. For each unformed bend b, rotate b's subtree by -sweep_b about b's axis, and replace b's cylinder with a flat strip. The strip length should be the neutral arc alpha*(Ri+K*t) when K is known; otherwise use the skin arc and flag about alpha*K*t uncertainty.
  4. Formed bends keep identity.
  This generalises _child_transform, where the per-link transform is unfold if unformed and identity if formed. It needs no full-skin proof (no seam closure, overlap or hole certificates). Mid-sequence sheets can self-intersect, but that is physically valid, so overlap checks must be off for intermediates.
- Method B (when a flat is uploaded and bound): fold the flat. Start from the panel tree and fold bends 1..k about their bend lines using nominal angle and radius from CAD, positioned by BA, then extrude by t. This works where CAD development refuses and is exact for the blank.
- Method C: use (a)'s _develop_faces transforms directly, but only on the 6/20 parts.
- Engine use: register the scan to each S_k and pick k by residual with margin, or take k from the scan job when the robot cell knows it. Then measure only bends 1..k against S_k's expected flange length, angle and bend-line position. Replace the order-free Poisson count with this prefix likelihood.

implications_for_production: No uploaded flat pattern is supported today. Every flat view is derived from the folded STEP, and only 6/20 corpus parts and 3/5 fresh uploads develop. A flat upload slot with a general DXF/GEO/flat-STEP parser is real missing scope, not a UI toggle.

The folded/unfolded toggle, order and מהלך-group parity across views, and flat PDF export already exist (VendorSetupPage.tsx:555-563, vendorUnfoldDraft.ts). An uploaded flat can feed the same VendorUnfoldPreview contract once its bend lines are bound to feature_ids. That needs a new binding step: panel-tree graph match plus 2D ICP plus operator confirmation, replacing the current exact-endpoint rule.

Intermediate expected geometry for incomplete scans should be built by hinge-rotating the subtrees of unformed bends of the folded CAD about the extracted bend axes. That uses 94% bend capture and does not depend on the 6/20 full-unfold gate. Folding the uploaded flat is the fallback. Requiring certified full skin development would leave about 70% of parts with no stage geometry.

Restrict partial-state hypotheses to prefixes of the tagged order at מהלך boundaries (at most n+1), and replace the order-free Poisson-binomial count in bend_unary_model.py:683-741 with residual-based stage selection. Better still, receive k from the Zeiss robot cell.

Skin-development lengths differ from the real blank by alpha*K*t per bend (about 1 mm at 90 deg, t=1.5). Unformed-bend strips and flat-to-CAD matching must use neutral-axis BA or a shop K. A real shop DXF lets us back-solve that K and gives an independent expected flange length where vendor_flange_preview returns null.

The available flats are reverse-engineered from the folded CAD, so they cannot validate flat ingestion or binding (circular). Collect real TruTops/BendMaster DXFs from the shop before claiming any gain.
Unfold V5/V6 and the FreeCAD manufacturing path are not wired into the API. Only workers v1-v4 are, behind the SHERMAN_VENDOR_UNFOLD_RUNTIME env var. Treat V5/V6/FreeCAD as research assets.
